group_assessment.weighting: Academic clinical-genomics centre reporting consecutive paediatric epilepsy diagnostics; no WWOX-focused publication, but the cohort carries four WWOX-diagnosed individuals and one cDNA-level splice result.

field_density.note: No PubMed record pairs WWOX with the phrase 'deep intronic'; this cohort reports a homozygous deep intronic WWOX variant with a cDNA consequence.

queued.why: Re-read 2026-10-04 (wave 11, Scientist B): reference 11, which the Methods name as the earlier publication of a subset of this cohort, carries the homozygous WWOX c.965A>G p.(His322Arg) allele in its Supplementary Table S7 (gene and variant only, no phenotype). Only the Table S7 row was inspected (artefacts held in the root corpus); the paper itself is unread.

entries.proposition: A homozygous WWOX c.107+119C>G deep intronic variant was shown by cDNA analysis to cause inclusion of the first intron in NM_016373, producing a premature stop codon.
entries.snippet: A homozygous WWOX c.107 + 119C>G variant was shown to lead to the inclusion of the first intron in transcript NM_016373 , leading to a premature stop codon after cDNA analysis.
entries.anchor: Results, Diagnostic variants (deep intronic variants paragraph)

entries.proposition: WWOX accounts for four of the fifty-one solved individuals with infantile epileptic spasms syndrome in this cohort, behind STXBP1 (6) and level with CDKL5 (4).
entries.snippet: Infantile epileptic spasms syndrome 51/132 (38.6%) STXBP1 (6), CDKL5 (4), WWOX (4)
entries.anchor: Table 1, Infantile epileptic spasms syndrome row

entries.proposition: The denominator: 733 families with paediatric epilepsy received clinical genome or exome sequencing, and 278 of 733 (37.9%) received a molecular diagnosis.
entries.snippet: A genetic diagnosis was identified in 278 of 733 individuals (37.9%;

entries.proposition: Cohort-level mortality at review was 9.3%, the comparator any WWOX mortality figure needs.
entries.snippet: Sixty‐eight individuals were deceased (9.3%) at the time of review.

entries.proposition: The four WWOX individuals carry three distinct biallelic genotypes, all homozygous with both parents as carriers, all with infantile epileptic spasms syndrome: a nonsense allele, a missense allele in two individuals of the same family, and the deep intronic allele.
entries.snippet: Hom	WWOX	c.107+119C>G	NM_016373	Maternal, Paternal
entries.anchor: Supplementary Table S9 (solved individuals), WWOX rows

entries.proposition: The deep intronic WWOX case was alive at review, while the two individuals sharing the homozygous missense genotype were recorded as deceased.
entries.snippet: Hom	WWOX	c.965A>G, p.(His322Arg)	NM_016373	Maternal
entries.anchor: Supplementary Table S9 (solved individuals), WWOX rows with mortality column

entries.proposition: Autosomal recessive homozygous inheritance accounts for 32 of 281 etiologies in this cohort, the band WWOX belongs to.
entries.snippet: followed by AD inherited (41/281, 14.6%) and autosomal recessive homozygous (32/281, 11.4%)

entries.proposition: Wave-11 re-read: the solved-cases table carries the homozygous WWOX missense allele c.965A>G p.(His322Arg) in two individuals (rows 150 and 151) who share consanguinity and a positive first-degree family history, both with focal seizures, abnormal MRI, global developmental delay and hypotonia, both deceased, both IESS.
entries.snippet: focal HP:0007359	yes	global developmental delay HP:0001263, hypotonia HP:0001252	deceased	IESS	Hom	WWOX	c.965A>G, p.(His322Arg)
entries.anchor: Supplementary Table S9 (solved individuals), rows id 150 and 151

entries.proposition: The authors kept VUS-carrying patients unsolved; the His322Arg family sits in the solved table, so the authors counted the allele as diagnostic although the held ClinVar snapshot classifies it as uncertain significance.
entries.snippet: These patients were, however, considered unsolved, as these VUS lacked sufficient evidence to upgrade their status according to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics guidelines.

entries.snippet: A subset of the current cohort was previously published without detailed phenotypic analyses, in a broader study of GMCK‐RD patients.
